summary_oneline: Add partial-matching dict operators (like, ilike, startswith, endswith, contains, regex) to the WHERE builders

localization.role: operator allowlist for dict filter values (extend)
Cython dict-value renderer (add new operator branch)
must exempt new operators from implicit JSONB containment
Rust fast-path twin of the Cython branch
pre-dispatch hook: pre-quotes dict value; candidate for operator validation
existing startswith/contains/endswith→ILIKE semantics and escaping helper to reuse

constraints.title: Two builders per dialect
constraints.text: Every operator added to pgsql.pyx must be mirrored in rust/src/pgsql_parser.rs (and sql.pyx ↔ sql_parser.rs); tests run both paths and skip Rust when the installed extension is stale.

constraints.title: JSONB dispatch runs first
constraints.text: jsonb_condition treats a dict without known operator keys as implicit containment; new operator names must be exempted there (Cython and Rust).

constraints.title: Rust errors are swallowed on pgsql
constraints.text: pgSQLParser.filter_conditions catches every Rust exception and re-renders via Cython, so a user-facing validation error must be raised before dispatch or identically in the Cython path.

constraints.title: is_valid pre-quoting invariant
constraints.text: _where_element wraps the dict operand in single quotes (and doubles embedded quotes) before builders run; builders must strip, then escape LIKE metacharacters, then quote via pg_literal.

constraints.title: Single operator per dict
constraints.text: _where_element keeps only the last (op, v) pair; Rust reads the first entry. Multi-key dicts are not a supported form for these operators.

constraints.title: Existing vocabulary
constraints.text: qsurl (translate.py) and DataFrame filters (types/dt/filters.py) already use startswith/endswith/contains/regex names with ILIKE semantics and a like_escape helper; parser-level operators should match.

whats_new: Partial-matching operator vocabulary as the single key of a dict-typed where_cond/filter value: like, ilike, startswith, istartswith, endswith, iendswith, contains, icontains, regex, iregex, each with a not_ twin. Plain names are case-sensitive, i* names case-insensitive (ILIKE on PostgreSQL, LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER(pattern) elsewhere). Regex (~, ~*, !~, !~*) is PostgreSQL-only.
A pre-dispatch validator raising ParserError when a contains operand is shorter than 3 characters (and for non-string operands).
A shared LIKE-metacharacter escaping helper usable from Cython (and a Rust twin).

what_changes.change: extend allowlist; add branch rendering LIKE/ILIKE/~ with strip→escape→wildcard→pg_literal; exempt in jsonb_condition
validate operator/operand before pre-quoting (contains min length) so the error is raised on both paths
LIKE-based operators plus LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER(...) for i* variants; regex raises ParserError
new dict-value branch (Dict variant in FilterValue) rendering LIKE/LOWER() forms with explicit ESCAPE '\\'
extend COMPARISON_TOKENS-only dict branch with LIKE/LOWER() forms via bq_quote_string
dual-path tests per operator incl. escaping and error cases

non_goals: qsurl grammar changes (qsurl already maps text expressions to ILIKE; regex pushdown capability stays out unless decided in spec).
Non-SQL dialects (CQL, Mongo, Elastic, ArangoDB, Rethink, Influx); regex on dialects other than PostgreSQL.
Changing the legacy `field~` key-suffix prefix-match behaviour.

patterns_to_follow.pattern: FEAT-152 ILIKE branch: strip is_valid pre-quote → pg_literal; identical comment block in Cython and Rust
like_escape from qsurl/translate.py for %, _ and \ escaping before adding wildcards
pytest.param with skipif on stale extension; render via _rs.pgsql_filter_conditions and _filter_conditions_cy

integration_risks.risk: Operator name collision with JSONB implicit containment: a user filtering a JSONB column by a key literally named 'contains' would change behaviour.
integration_risks.mitigation: document reserved operator names; exemption only applies when the single key is a reserved operator and the operand is a string

integration_risks.risk: Error raised inside Rust is silently swallowed on pgsql; tests on the Rust path alone would pass while the user sees no error.
integration_risks.mitigation: raise in _where_element (pre-dispatch) and assert on the full parser flow in tests

integration_risks.risk: Unbounded user regex pushed to PostgreSQL may be expensive (ReDoS-like); residual.py already guards pattern length for in-memory regex.
Stale .so: tests see old Rust code unless make build-rust + stage-rust run.

claims.claim: Dict-typed where_cond values are rendered in filter_conditions of sql.pyx / pgsql.pyx, each with a Rust fast path and a Cython fallback
pgsql already exposes the extension point for text operators (PG_TEXT_OPERATORS: ILIKE/NOT ILIKE) in both Cython and Rust
New operator names must be exempted in jsonb_condition or the dict is rendered as JSONB containment
claims.reasoning: operators==0 branch renders col @> json; FEAT-152 needed the same exemption

claims.claim: pgsql Rust-path exceptions are swallowed, so the 'contains too short' error must be raised pre-dispatch or in Cython as well
claims.reasoning: bare except Exception: pass at pgsql.pyx:311

claims.claim: Dict operands arrive pre-quoted by is_valid; builders must strip before escaping and quoting
claims.reasoning: pinned invariant (commit f313e115) and strip code in both builders

claims.claim: qsurl already defines startswith/contains/endswith → ILIKE with like_escape; parser-level operators can reuse it
Generic SQL, mssql and BigQuery builders have no text-operator support; extending them is new work
claims.reasoning: no LIKE handling found; mssql has no dict variant at all

claims.claim: _where_element is the right single hook for pre-dispatch validation
claims.reasoning: runs before both builders; but it currently never raises, so behaviour change is a design decision

claims.claim: Tests must be dual-path with a stale-extension skip, and the .so must be rebuilt/staged
claims.reasoning: existing test file and memory note

claims.claim: Legacy key-suffix form field~ already gives case-insensitive prefix match and must keep working
claims.reasoning: code present in both builders; no tests located for it

claims.claim: Pushing user regex to PostgreSQL needs a safety bound
claims.reasoning: inferred from residual.py precedent; no DB-side evidence gathered

unknowns.question: Are startswith / endswith / contains case-insensitive (ILIKE, as qsurl does today) or case-sensitive (LIKE)?
plausible_answers: a) case-insensitive ILIKE for all three (qsurl parity) — recommended
b) case-sensitive LIKE; users use ilike for insensitive
unknowns.user_answer: Both variants: plain names case-sensitive (LIKE), i-prefixed names case-insensitive (ILIKE / LOWER()).

unknowns.question: Which dialects are in scope: PostgreSQL only, or also the generic SQLParser (MySQL/SQLite via LIKE) in the same feature?
plausible_answers: a) PostgreSQL (Rust+Cython) plus generic SQLParser with LIKE-only ops; regex PG-only — recommended
c) all SQL dialects incl. SQL Server and BigQuery
unknowns.user_answer: All SQL dialects: PostgreSQL, generic SQLParser, SQL Server, BigQuery (Cython + Rust). Regex PostgreSQL-only.

unknowns.question: regex semantics: map `regex` to case-sensitive `~`, case-insensitive `~*`, or offer both (`regex` / `iregex`)? Should negations (`not_regex`) and a max pattern length apply?
plausible_answers: a) regex→~, iregex→~*, not_regex→!~, bounded length — recommended
unknowns.user_answer: regex→~, iregex→~*, not_regex→!~ (not_iregex→!~*), bounded pattern length.

unknowns.question: Does the minimum-length (≥3) rule apply only to contains, or to every partial-matching operator? Which exception: ParserError (QueryException subclass)?
plausible_answers: a) contains only, raise ParserError before dispatch — recommended
unknowns.user_answer: contains only (and i/not_ forms); ParserError raised pre-dispatch in _where_element.

unknowns.question: Include the negated family (not_contains, not_startswith, not_endswith, not_like, not_ilike) in this feature?
plausible_answers: a) yes, full not_* family (qsurl and dt/filters parity) — recommended
unknowns.user_answer: Full not_* family for every operator.

unknowns.question: How should the case-insensitive i* variants render on dialects without ILIKE (generic SQL/MySQL, SQL Server, BigQuery)?
plausible_answers: b) plain LIKE, rely on collation
unknowns.user_answer: LOWER(col) LIKE LOWER(pattern), explicit and collation-independent.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and all six open questions are resolved; the change extends the FEAT-152 ILIKE extension point plus a pre-dispatch validator. The four-dialect scope is large but mechanical: the spec should define one shared operator table and escaping helper and decompose per dialect with Cython/Rust twins.
